title: 2016 AMC 8 Problem 25
statement: A semicircle is inscribed in an isosceles triangle with base \(16\) and height \(15\) so that the diameter of the semicircle is contained in the base of the triangle as shown. What is the radius of the semicircle?

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center of the circle, which is the midpoint of \(\overline{AB}.\)

We then get that \(BC = 17\) via the Pythagorean theorem.

The right half of the isosceles triangle has area \[[\triangle BOC]=\dfrac12\cdot8\cdot15=60.\] The radius \(OE\) is perpendicular to the tangent side \(BC\), so the same area is \(\dfrac12\cdot OE\cdot17.\) Hence \[OE=\dfrac{120}{17}.\]

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Draw the radius to the point where the semicircle touches a side of the triangle.
Compare the area of the right half of the triangle using two different bases.
